question: Is one Bismillah enough for a whole batch of machine-slaughtered chickens?
answer:
A lot of people say: what do we do with the large-scale meat processing, and the chickens that are slaughtered by the machines, and the saying of the Bismillah and whatnot? And this is something that I don't have an easy answer for. Obviously, in the good old days, you would say Bismillah for every animal. In our modern times, you cannot say Bismillah for every single chicken. I mean, to put it bluntly, if you want your chicken nuggets, you're going to have to have chicken manufacturing plants; it's either/or, right? If you want to just buy your packet of chicken nuggets, you're going to have to have these massive plants where 100,000 chickens are processed in two, three hours. You can't have the Bismillah over every single one of them. All I can say is that some Bismillah is better than nothing.

And I'll quote you the Majma' al-Fiqh in Jeddah, 1997, the Global Fiqh Council, which I respect immensely. In 1997 they came together for this issue, and in the fatwa they released, and I'll quote you with this, we conclude: for any animal to be permissible, three conditions must be met. Number one, the one who slaughters is a Muslim or a Kitabi. Number two, the instrument is sharp and spills blood. And number three, the name of Allah must be mentioned; but if the person forgot, then it is forgiven. That's a different thing, to be intentional or unintentional.

And then they said that for chicken slaughterhouses, one Bismillah for every batch of continuous chickens is permissible, but they said it must be a human, and not a tape recorder or some type of iPhone or something. So one Bismillah that is said by a person, a Kitabi or a Muslim. If it's a Kitabi, they can say "in the name of God," or they can say it in Hebrew; it doesn't matter. It does not have to be in Arabic, any language, but they have to say the name of Allah.

And you know, I understand our Deobandi brothers, our Hanafi brothers; they say it must be a Bismillah for every single chicken, and I respect that. Good for them. Me personally, I am happy with this fatwa that says one Bismillah, even for a batch, as long as it's continuous. So the point is that when you start the machine, you say Bismillah, and your niyyah is that, as long as it is continuously running, with that Bismillah I want this entire batch of chickens to be slaughtered. Inshallah, at least some Bismillah is said, and I'm sympathetic to this, even though I respect the other position as well.
